name: Video Editing Skill
description: Deterministic video editing: typed edit requests (trim, cut, concat with transitions, speed, fit/fill/resize, rotate/flip, image overlay, freeze frame, reverse, still image to clip) compiled to an operation graph with source/timeline mapping and executed through ffmpeg-skill. Not an agent: no editing decisions, no LLM, no commands.

unsupported.reason: free placement of a video layer (picture-in-picture, chroma key) is motion-graphics-skill's video_overlay, not an operation here: OVERLAY composites still images only (ADR-035)

tools.description: join two or more inputs in order, optionally with a transition, conforming size / fps

parameters.transition: {type: fade|dissolve|wipeleft|wiperight|wipeup|wipedown|slideleft|slideright|circleopen|circleclose|fadeblack|fadewhite|smoothleft|smoothright|radial, duration: time 0.01..10} (optional), or {type: stinger, stinger: video source id (a file with alpha), cut_point: time (the frame the clips switch at), cover: {start, end} (the window the graphic covers the whole frame; must contain cut_point)} (contract.stinger)
parameters.mode: pad | crop (how inputs of another aspect reach the frame)

media.inputs: two or more videos (any sizes / frame rates; conformed by params.mode to params.width/height/fps or the first input)

output.frame_size: params.width x params.height, else the first input
output.fps: params.fps, else the first input; constant, with every input joined at whole frames of it (with or without a transition: an input at another rate or variable-rate is conformed to it, rounded to the nearest frame; one at that rate whose length is not whole frames is cut, rounded down; an xfade transition's duration is rounded to the nearest frame; the timeline places every clip at those lengths)
output.audio: stereo AAC when any input has audio (silence is inserted for inputs without); none when no input has audio

tools.description: apply a rule per labelled span (cut, keep, or speed by a factor) and keep everything else by params.default: approved proposals (retakes, silences, static spans) become segments here

parameters.segments: [{start, end, label}] non-overlapping spans of the input (e.g. approved proposals: retake, silence, static); label [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_+.-]{0,39}
parameters.rules: {label: cut | keep | {speed: factor 1/4..4, not 1}}: one per label used
parameters.default: cut | keep | {speed: factor} for the time no segment covers (default keep)
parameters.output: result (default: the edit) | removed (a review file: only the spans the rules cut, joined in order at speed 1; the record lists each with its place in the file)

output.audio: kept (stereo AAC: the pieces are joined by ffmpeg-skill/join); sped-up pieces keep their pitch (atempo)
output.duration: the kept time plus each sped span's length / its factor

tools.description: keep exactly the pixel rectangle {x, y, width, height} the caller gives (no scaling, padding or aspect maths; FILL crops to an aspect ratio)

parameters.x: int px >= 0: left edge in the input frame as displayed
parameters.width: even int px: the rectangle's width (x + width <= input width)
parameters.height: even int px: the rectangle's height (y + height <= input height)

tools.description: keep several ranges of one input, joined in the order given (removes everything else)
centre-crop into an aspect ratio (edges are lost)

parameters.anchor: {x, y} each 0..1: which edge the crop keeps (0=left/top, 0.5=centre default, 1=right/bottom) (optional)

tools.description: letterbox / pillarbox into an aspect ratio (nothing is cropped)

output.frame_size: params.aspect (params.width when given; padded, nothing cropped)

tools.description: hold one frame for a number of seconds: at a time (the rest of the clip plays on after the hold) or, without one, the last frame at the end

parameters.hold: time 0.01..600 s: how long the frame is held
parameters.at: time, < input duration (optional): hold the frame shown at `at` and play the rest after the hold; omitted: hold the last frame at the end

output.audio: as input, silent during the hold
output.duration: input duration + params.hold (the hold is a whole number of frames when params.at is given)

tools.description: turn a still image (title card, end slate) into a silent video clip of a set duration that CONCAT and every other type can take

parameters.width: even int px (optional; alone: height follows the image aspect)
parameters.height: even int px (optional; alone: width follows the image aspect; both: exact frame, the image covers it, centre-cropped)

media.inputs: one image source (png / jpg), never a video or an operation

output.frame_size: params.width x params.height; only one given -> the other from the image aspect; none -> the image size (each even; the image is scaled to cover the frame and centre-cropped, never stretched)
output.audio: none (a silent clip: CONCAT inserts silence for it next to inputs with audio)

tools.description: composite a still image (logo, lower-third PNG) at a named position for a time range; a video layer, picture-in-picture or chroma key is motion-graphics-skill's video_overlay (ADR-035)

parameters.image: image source id (png / jpg); a video source or an operation is INVALID_INPUT overlay_video_layer: use motion-graphics-skill video_overlay

media.inputs: one video plus one image source (png / jpg; alpha respected)

tools.description: zoom in by a scale on a subject box the caller gives (e.g. detection-skill's face box) for a time range: a hard cut in and out, the window centred on the box and kept inside the frame, the frame size unchanged

parameters.end: time (> start): the zoomed range; a hard cut in at start and out at end
parameters.scale: number or N/D in (1, 4]: the zoom (2 = the window is half the frame in each dimension)
parameters.subject: {x, y, width, height} int px in the input frame as displayed: the box to keep in view (e.g. detection-skill's face box); the window is centred on it and kept inside the frame

output.audio: kept (stereo AAC: the parts are joined by ffmpeg-skill/join)

tools.description: scale to a width keeping the aspect ratio

output.frame_size: params.width, height by the input aspect (even)

tools.description: play the input backwards, picture and audio

media.inputs: one video (the engine buffers the whole input in memory: keep it short, TRIM first)

tools.description: turn the picture clockwise by 90/180/270 and/or mirror it horizontally or vertically (no scaling, padding or cropping)

parameters.flip: h | v, mirror horizontal/vertical (optional; at least one of degrees/flip is required)

output.frame_size: as input, with width and height swapped when params.degrees is 90 or 270

tools.description: retime by a constant factor (video and pitch-preserved audio)

parameters.smooth: blend | interpolate (optional; slow-motion quality when factor < 1 -- ffmpeg-skill fit.py ignores it when speeding up)

tools.description: keep one source time range [start, end)

parameters.precision: frame (default, re-encode) | keyframe (lossless when possible) | auto (stream copy when the copy lands within 0.2 s of the range, e.g. an in point on a keyframe; else a frame-accurate re-encode; reported per cut) | smart (frame-accurate; only the partial GOPs at each cut point re-encoded, the whole GOPs between copied, verified against the source; else the whole cut re-encoded, with the reason; contract.smart_cut)

parameters.transition: {type: fade|dissolve|wipeleft|wiperight|wipeup|wipedown|slideleft|slideright|circleopen|circleclose|fadeblack|fadewhite|smoothleft|smoothright|radial, duration: time 0.01..10} (optional), or {type: stinger, stinger: video source id (a file with alpha), cut_point: time (the frame the clips switch at), cover: {start, end} (the window the graphic covers the whole frame; must contain cut_point)} (contract.stinger)
parameters.mode: pad | crop (how inputs of another aspect reach the frame)

parameters.segments: [{start, end, label}] non-overlapping spans of the input (e.g. approved proposals: retake, silence, static); label [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_+.-]{0,39}
parameters.rules: {label: cut | keep | {speed: factor 1/4..4, not 1}}: one per label used
parameters.default: cut | keep | {speed: factor} for the time no segment covers (default keep)
parameters.output: result (default: the edit) | removed (a review file: only the spans the rules cut, joined in order at speed 1; the record lists each with its place in the file)

parameters.x: int px >= 0: left edge in the input frame as displayed
parameters.width: even int px: the rectangle's width (x + width <= input width)
parameters.height: even int px: the rectangle's height (y + height <= input height)

parameters.anchor: {x, y} each 0..1: which edge the crop keeps (0=left/top, 0.5=centre default, 1=right/bottom) (optional)

parameters.hold: time 0.01..600 s: how long the frame is held
parameters.at: time, < input duration (optional): hold the frame shown at `at` and play the rest after the hold; omitted: hold the last frame at the end

parameters.width: even int px (optional; alone: height follows the image aspect)
parameters.height: even int px (optional; alone: width follows the image aspect; both: exact frame, the image covers it, centre-cropped)

parameters.image: image source id (png / jpg); a video source or an operation is INVALID_INPUT overlay_video_layer: use motion-graphics-skill video_overlay

parameters.end: time (> start): the zoomed range; a hard cut in at start and out at end
parameters.scale: number or N/D in (1, 4]: the zoom (2 = the window is half the frame in each dimension)
parameters.subject: {x, y, width, height} int px in the input frame as displayed: the box to keep in view (e.g. detection-skill's face box); the window is centred on it and kept inside the frame

parameters.flip: h | v, mirror horizontal/vertical (optional; at least one of degrees/flip is required)

parameters.smooth: blend | interpolate (optional; slow-motion quality when factor < 1 -- ffmpeg-skill fit.py ignores it when speeding up)

engine.invocation: [python, <ffmpeg-skill>/scripts/<tool>.py, typed argv, --json]; process group; scrubbed env; timeout

detected: CLI flags per tool (scripts/_contract.py --json input_schema, else <tool>.py --help)
optional tools (tools_optional): a checkout without one leaves only the operation it executes MISSING
the ffmpeg-skill tool of each unsupported type (doctor: unsupported[].engine_tool_status)
encoding quality flag: --quality where offered, else --crf (same CRF scale)
probe colour key: video.bt2020_or_hdr where present, else video.hdr (same meaning)
cut.py's SDR HEVC re-encode codec: --no-keep-hevc passed where offered (3.0+), so a frame-precision TRIM / CUT writes H.264 for SDR like every other operation
cut.py --smart (3.2.3+): a precision smart TRIM / CUT uses it where offered, else --accurate (contract.smart_cut)
compatibility.floor_reason: overlay.py bounds a looped-image composite with -t only from 0.10.0 (behaviour, not a flag)

execution.stdin: EditRequest JSON when the request argument is '-'
execution.stdout: exactly one response document when --json is given
execution.stderr: diagnostics only; never part of the contract
execution.executable_resolution: ffmpeg-skill directory from environment / CLI only; ffmpeg and ffprobe from PATH by ffmpeg-skill; nothing from the request
execution.output_location: request output paths are relative to --workspace and may not leave it
execution.dry_run: plan - --json compiles, checks ranges against probed durations and asks ffmpeg-skill --dry-run for commands; no media is written

sources.ai_generated: optional {generator, licence}: the caller declares the source AI-generated (contract.ai_generated)

outputs.encoding: optional {crf, preset} (contract.encoding); refused where noted there
outputs.max_size: optional {bytes | kb | mb | gb | kib | mib | gib: number} (MB = 10^6 bytes): fit the file under it (contract.size_limit)

options.segment_cache: bool (default false): a frame-precision CUT renders each keep range alone, cached by content, joined by stream copy (contract.segment_cache)

time.representation: exact rationals; serialised as {seconds: 'fixed 6 places', rational: 'N/D'}
time.mapping: every output carries a timeline: tracks[].segments[] with source_range and timeline_range per source

identity.operation_id: op_ + sha256(type, canonical params, input identities)[:16]; input identity = sha256 of source bytes or upstream operation_id
identity.idempotency_key: sha256(operation_id, tool, tool versions, skill version, container)
identity.reuse: a work-dir intermediate whose record matches the idempotency key and hash is reused and reported status: reused

provenance.observation: probe documents are OBSERVED with source ffmpeg-skill/probe@<version>; request values are never reported as observations

graph.model: sources -> operations (DAG) -> outputs; every operation feeds an output; order is topological, ties by id
refused: cycle (DEPENDENCY_ERROR)
unknown input / operation reference (DEPENDENCY_ERROR)
duplicate source / operation / output id (INVALID_REQUEST)
operation that leads to no output (DEPENDENCY_ERROR)
two outputs on one path (DEPENDENCY_ERROR)
video slot fed by an image or image slot fed by a video / operation (DEPENDENCY_ERROR)
unknown operation type (UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION)
unknown or forbidden key anywhere (INVALID_REQUEST)
media an operation cannot take (INVALID_INPUT, before execution)
engine tool / encoder / filter missing (TOOL_ERROR, before execution)

before_execution: every source probed by ffmpeg-skill (video: stream + duration; image: decodes)
after_each_operation: probe: video stream, duration, frame size
duration within tolerance of the timeline (frame / auto / smart 0.35 s, keyframe 1.5 s)
frame size / aspect / width as requested, or equal to the input for TRIM / CUT / SPEED / OVERLAY / FREEZE / REVERSE
frame rate as requested (a CONCAT without a transition or with a stinger: the first input's when params.fps is not given)
audio stream kept when the input(s) had one
validation.on_reuse: the candidate is re-validated with the same checks (hash, size, probe); a stale record is discarded and the operation runs again
validation.response: every document is checked against the response shape before it is printed (self-check); a violation is INTERNAL_ERROR

doctor_shape.engine: ffmpeg-skill location, version, ffmpeg / ffprobe, missing capabilities
doctor_shape.supported_operations: types whose status is AVAILABLE (never a guess)

versioning.rule: two independent axes (docs/decisions.md ADR-007): `version` is this package's own release version and may move on any release, including one that changes nothing a dependent needs to react to; `contract_version` is the version of the shape a pinned block publishes and changes only when a pinned block changes in a breaking way. A change inside a pinned block bumps `contract_version` (and `version`, since this package does not yet release independently of its contract) and agents must re-pin; new keys outside the pinned blocks (top level or inside tools[]) are additive and allowed within the same contract_version; the golden copy tests/contract/contract.json is regenerated deliberately in the same change, and `contract --check` classifies every difference as breaking or additive

0.7.0: RESIZE: `height` as the alternative to `width` -- blocked on ffmpeg-skill: `fit.py` has no `--height` flag (docs/decisions.md ADR-003 correction, found by live verification against ffmpeg-skill 0.10.0)
stabilize / sequence / background: capability ownership (here, elsewhere, or nowhere) not yet decided (see kajisho5/video-editing-skill#11 item 3)
POSITION: not planned as a type (see docs/decisions.md ADR-002)
OVERLAY video layer / chroma key: not planned; motion-graphics-skill video_overlay owns it (docs/decisions.md ADR-035)

parameters.crf: integer 14..28: x264 constant-quality factor (lower = larger, better; engine default 18; +2 on HEVC for HDR sources)
parameters.preset: ultrafast|superfast|veryfast|faster|fast|medium|slow|slower|veryslow (encoder speed / efficiency trade-off; engine default medium)

encoding.applies_to: the operation that produces the output: its re-encode uses the profile; an intermediate feeding two outputs must be asked for one profile
encoding.identity: part of operation_id and idempotency_key when present, so a different profile is a different artifact

fixed_by_engine.video_codec: h264 (libx264, High, yuv420p, bt709 tags) for SDR sources; hevc (libx265, 10-bit, hvc1) for HDR sources
fixed_by_engine.audio_codec: aac 192 kb/s, source sample rate and layout (CONCAT: stereo)
fixed_by_engine.resolution: by RESIZE / FIT / FILL / CONCAT (frame_semantics), never by the profile
fixed_by_engine.frame_rate: by params.fps of CONCAT / FIT / FILL / RESIZE; VFR sources are conformed to CFR

not_configurable: audio codec, bitrate, sample rate, channel layout
refused: unknown keys (INVALID_REQUEST)
crf or preset outside the vocabulary (INVALID_REQUEST)
a profile on an output produced by TRIM / CUT with precision keyframe, auto or smart: stream copy ignores it (INVALID_REQUEST)
two outputs of one operation with different profiles (DEPENDENCY_ERROR)

size_limit.request_field: project.outputs[].max_size: {mb: 25} (one of bytes, kb, mb, gb = 10^3 steps; kib, mib, gib = 2^10 steps); 100 kB .. 50 GB
size_limit.engine: ffmpeg-skill/export --preset youtube --no-scale --allow-long --max-mb <target MiB>: a two-pass x264 encode at the video bitrate the running time leaves after the audio (AAC 192k), at the produced frame size and rate
size_limit.retry: measured after each encode: over the limit -> target x limit / size x 0.97; under 90 % -> target x 0.95 x limit / size; up to 5 encodes; the delivered file lies in [90 %, 100 %] of the limit
refused: with outputs[].encoding (a quality and a size: give one; INVALID_REQUEST size_and_encoding)
a path that is not .mp4 (INVALID_REQUEST size_needs_mp4)
an ffmpeg-skill without export --max-mb (2.x+; TOOL_ERROR before execution)

a limit the engine cannot meet (under its lowest watchable video bitrate, 100 kb/s, for the duration; or none of 5 encodes in range): OUTPUT_ERROR size_limit_unreachable with the attempts and the engine's reason; nothing is delivered
size_limit.not_done: no automatic downscale or audio-bitrate reduction to make a small limit fit: the failure says so and the caller decides
size_limit.report: execution.outputs[].size_limit: {limit_bytes, bytes, ratio, attempts: [{target_mib, bytes, ratio}], two_pass}

retakes.transcript: JSON file under an allowed root: {words: [{word | text, start, end}]} in time order
retakes.profile: en | ja (default en; others are regional profiles)

request_shape.source: the video silence / static measure (under an allowed root)
request_shape.static: {}: spans with no motion, the shots ffmpeg-skill/scenes --shots labels static

spans.silence: ffmpeg-skill/silence --list --threshold --min-silence: its silences, snapped to the source's frame grid
spans.static: ffmpeg-skill/scenes --shots: shots labelled static (a measured optical-flow proxy); the span edges are the shot boundaries the engine's scene detection finds, so a still span that starts or ends without a visible change of picture is found only at the shot's edges
spans.and: only where every asked measurement holds (silent and static); label silence+static
spans.or: wherever any holds; labelled with every measurement that touches the span
spans.needs: ffmpeg-skill silence.py; scenes.py --shots (2.x+, detected; TOOL_ERROR without it)

proposals.applies: nothing: the response says applied: false; approved proposal ids become CONDENSE segments, and only those are cut

rules.repeat: the same 1-4 words twice in a row; the first saying is proposed, up to where the second starts
rules.restart: a phrase of 2+ words said again within 8 words and 4 s, with only hesitations between (or a 3+ word opening after at most 3 words)
rules.fragment: a broken-off word (ends with -, —, ~) or a short false start the next word begins with

confidence.meaning: a fixed weight of the rule that fired, not a probability; emphatic doubles of the profile (very very, はい はい) score below the default

not_provided: any model, score or language detection

stinger.request_field: CONCAT params.transition: {type: stinger, stinger, cut_point, cover: {start, end}}
stinger.file: a video source with an alpha plane (ProRes 4444, QuickTime Animation, PNG in MOV, ...), the edit's aspect and frame rate; its length is the file's; its sound, if any, is mixed in. hyperframes-skill / remotion-ffmpeg-skill / blender-skill write one with its stinger.json: cut_point and cover come from it (the caller reads it and passes them)
stinger.placement: the clips are butt-joined; at each join the cut is the first frame of the next clip, and the stinger starts cut_point before it, so its frame at cut_point lies on the cut frame; every clip is joined at whole frames of the edit's rate, as in a plain CONCAT (a clip at that rate rounded down, one at another rate or variable-rate conformed to it, rounded to the nearest frame), so every cut is on a frame
engine_calls: ffmpeg-skill/look <stinger> --at <a quarter frame before cut_point> --width <its width> --no-timecode -o <png>, once before anything runs: the stinger's frame at cut_point, written with its alpha (cover_check)
ffmpeg-skill/fit --fps <edit rate> --duration <whole frames> --method trim, for a clip at another rate or variable-rate
ffmpeg-skill/cut --start 0 --end <whole frames> --accurate, only for a clip whose measured length is not that (a stream-copied segment, as a rule)
ffmpeg-skill/join (no transition, the CONCAT's size / rate / mode)
with sound: ffmpeg-skill/broll --insert <stinger> --at <start> --duration <length> --audio mix per join, then ffmpeg-skill/audio --replace (that mix onto the composite)
refused: no cut_point (INVALID_REQUEST stinger_no_cut_point) or no cover (INVALID_REQUEST stinger_no_cover)
cut_point outside cover (INVALID_REQUEST stinger_not_covering)
cut_point not on a frame of the stinger (INVALID_REQUEST cut_point_not_on_frame)

a stinger whose frame at cut_point is not opaque in every pixel, measured (INVALID_INPUT stinger_not_covering, details.measured), or whose alpha there cannot be read (INVALID_INPUT stinger_cover_unmeasured); before anything runs
a stinger without an alpha plane (INVALID_INPUT stinger_no_alpha), of another aspect (stinger_aspect) or frame rate (stinger_fps)
an input shorter than the stinger's lead-in (before the join) or tail (after it) (INVALID_TIME_RANGE)
a stinger that is an operation, not a source (DEPENDENCY_ERROR kind_mismatch)
an ffmpeg-skill without look.py --at / --no-timecode or overlay.py --place, or (stinger with sound) broll.py / audio.py --replace (TOOL_ERROR)
stinger.report: execution.operations[].stinger and plan.steps[].stinger: {source, cut_point, cover, duration, audio, joins: [{cut_at, stinger_start, stinger_end}], cover_check, cover_measured: {tool, frame, at, measured, covered, pixels, pixels_below, min_alpha, threshold, opaque_within, frame_size, provenance: OBSERVED} (in a plan: measured false, measured when the request runs)}; the output timeline's overlay track has a {kind: stinger, cut_at, timeline_range} segment per join
stinger.cover_check: declared and measured: the cover window (the stinger maker's statement) must contain cut_point, and the stinger's own frame at cut_point is measured before anything runs: ffmpeg-skill/look writes it as a PNG with its alpha, this Skill reads every pixel's alpha, and the frame covers when none is under 253 of 255 (ffmpeg-skill's alpha tolerance, 2 of 255); the same stinger and cut point are measured once per request

whole_frames.applies_to: every CONCAT: without a transition and with a stinger (contract.stinger) the inputs are butt-joined; with an xfade transition they overlap by its duration, held to whole frames too
whole_frames.rate: params.fps, else the first input's frame rate (as join.py chooses it); the output is constant at that rate
rule: every input is joined at whole frames of the rate, and the timeline places every clip at that length

an input at the rate: its planned length rounded down to whole frames (one within 1 ms of the next frame keeps it); cut to it (ffmpeg-skill/cut --start 0 --end <length> --accurate) only when its measured length differs (a stream-copied segment, a cut that kept a part frame), else joined as it is

an input at another rate, or variable-rate: its planned length rounded to the nearest frame of the rate, conformed to the rate and that length first (ffmpeg-skill/fit --fps <rate> --duration <length> --method trim); a clip rounded up holds its last instant for the rest of its last frame (a timeline segment of speed 0)

an xfade transition: its duration rounded to the nearest frame of the rate (a half up, at least one frame) and joined at that length (ffmpeg-skill/join --duration); the timeline overlaps the clips by it, so every clip starts on a frame
whole_frames.why: join.py trims each clip to its own length and starts the next after it: a length that is not whole frames of the output rate moved every later clip off the frame grid (a one-frame hole in the picture once the remainders reached half a frame, and a timeline that drifted from the file by the remainder of every clip). With an xfade, join.py starts each transition at the lengths before it less the transitions, and xfade starts one only on a frame: an offset between frames started the next clip's picture on the frame after it, up to a frame after its sound and its timeline place
whole_frames.report: execution.operations[].whole_frames and plan.steps[].whole_frames: {rate: {fps, rational}, inputs: [{input, fps, length, joined_length, action: none | cut | conform (a plan: cut_if_needed | conform | none), measured_length}], and with an xfade transition: {type, duration, joined_duration, frames}}; the join's own arguments (plan.steps[].arguments.duration) carry the joined duration
whole_frames.validation: the output's frame rate is the rate within 0.02, also when params.fps is not given (VALIDATION_ERROR fps)
refused: an input whose whole-frame length is no frame at all (INVALID_TIME_RANGE shorter_than_a_frame), before anything runs
with an xfade transition, an input whose whole-frame length is not longer than twice the joined transition (INVALID_TIME_RANGE), before anything runs
whole_frames.engine_note: join.py writes each clip's length to the millisecond and starts the next clip after the longer of its picture and its sound: a clip of whole frames whose length rounds up (at 30 fps a frame count 2 more than a multiple of 3, up by 1/3 ms; at 29.97 fps up to 0.5 ms) still starts the next one that much late, so some 35 to 50 such clips in one edit can still leave a one-frame hole; that remainder is the engine's (a proposal to ffmpeg-skill), not worked around here. With an xfade, join.py writes each transition's offset to the millisecond too, and xfade starts it on the first frame at or after that time: a whole-frame offset that rounds up (at 30, 24 or 60 fps one offset in three, at 29.97, 23.976 or 59.94 fps about one in two; never at 25 or 50 fps) starts that transition, and the next clip's picture, one frame late, against its sound and the timeline (not worked around here either). Before ffmpeg-skill 2.4.1 join.py does not trim a clip's sound to its picture, so an AAC tail can still start the next clip up to a frame late

ai_generated.request_field: project.sources[].ai_generated: {generator: text, licence: text} (each 1..200 printable characters)
ai_generated.meaning: declared by the caller, never inferred from the media; reported with provenance DECLARED
ai_generated.mark: AI_GENERATED: execution.operations[].marks / ai_generated and execution.outputs[].marks / ai_generated list every declared source the result contains ({source, generator, licence, provenance: DECLARED}); execution.sources[].ai_generated repeats the declaration
ai_generated.identity: not part of operation_id or idempotency_key: the bytes decide identity; the mark is recomputed on every run, so a reused result is marked too
normalisation: CONCAT conforms a generated clip with the rest (ffmpeg-skill/join): frame size by params.width / height (mode pad | crop), frame rate by params.fps or the first input's, square pixels (setsar=1), BT.709 tags on the H.264 output, and a silent track for an input without sound when another has sound
set params.width / height / fps on the CONCAT so the edit's format decides, not whichever clip comes first

segment_cache.applies_to: CUT with precision frame; every other type is one engine call and is reused as a whole (contract.identity.reuse)
render: each keep range is cut on its own: ffmpeg-skill/cut --start --end --accurate (plus the output's encoding profile)
each part is validated (video, duration within the frame tolerance, audio kept) and stored under <work>/segments/ with its record
the parts are joined by stream copy: ffmpeg-skill/join --transition none --copy (one part: copied as is)
segment_cache.segment_key: sha256(input identity, range start / end as rationals, tool, tool versions, skill version, container, encoding, engine release flags); the rest of the keep list is not part of it
segment_cache.partial_re_render: after a change only the parts whose key is new are encoded; the rest are taken from the cache (status reused)
segment_cache.same_request_twice: the operation itself is reused (idempotency_key); nothing is encoded or written in the work directory
segment_cache.report: execution.operations[].segments: {mode: segments, join: stream_copy | single | single_pass_fallback, parts: [{index, range, key, status: encoded | reused, sha256, seconds}], encoded, reused, fallback_reason?}; plan.steps[].segments: [{index, range, key, cached}]
differs_from_single_pass: the joins are butted: cut.py's declick fades (--segments) are not applied to a stream-copy join
the bytes differ from the single-pass render, so the idempotency key carries render: segments
segment_cache.fallback: when ffmpeg-skill refuses the copy join (the parts' picture and sound do not line up within its limit), the operation is rendered in one pass as without the cache; the parts stay cached and the record says single_pass_fallback with the engine's reason
segment_cache.needs: ffmpeg-skill/join --copy (from ffmpeg-skill 2.24.0, detected); without it a request asking for the cache is refused before execution (TOOL_ERROR)
segment_cache.reuse_false: options.reuse false also bypasses the segment cache (every part is encoded again and the cache is refreshed)

smart_cut.request_field: TRIM / CUT params.precision: smart (opt-in; the default stays frame)
smart_cut.what_it_does: a cut point between keyframes is re-encoded from that point to the next keyframe, and from the last keyframe to the end point; the whole GOPs between are the source's packets; the sound is cut on the picture's frame grid and encoded once (AAC). The engine checks the result against the source (frame count and grid, copied packets, decoded frames of each re-encoded part, stream parameters) before it is written; the result is frame-accurate like precision frame
smart_cut.engine_fallback: a source the engine cannot match (not H.264 8-bit 4:2:0 Baseline / Main / High, interlaced, variable-rate, HDR, an open GOP at a copy boundary, ...) or a check that fails: the engine re-encodes the whole cut (mode accurate) and says why (smart.reason, smart.reason_code, diagnostics.fallbacks); the operation still succeeds
smart_cut.engine_without_smart: an ffmpeg-skill whose cut.py has no --smart (detected; before 3.2.3): the cut runs as precision frame (--accurate), a warning is added, and the record says smart.applied false, reason_code engine_without_smart
refused: an outputs[].encoding profile on its output (INVALID_REQUEST encoding_needs_reencode): the copied GOPs keep the source's quality
not_applied: the cuts CONDENSE / PUNCH_IN / a stinger CONCAT make inside themselves (their result is re-encoded by the next step anyway)
smart_cut.validation: as precision frame: duration within 0.35 s, the input frame, audio kept, and the re-encode codec rule (H.264 for SDR)
smart_cut.report: execution.operations[].cuts: cut.py's mode (smart | accurate), reencoded, reencode_reason, duration_delta_seconds, ..., fallbacks (the engine's diagnostics.fallbacks) and smart: {applied, parts: [{segment, kind: reencode | copy, start, end, frames}], reencoded_frames, copied_frames, checks, source} or {applied: false, reason, reason_code, source}; plan.steps[].smart: {engine_flag: --smart | --accurate, available, reason_code, reason}

RESIZE.keeps: the source aspect ratio; nothing is padded, cropped or stretched
RESIZE.target: width = params.width (even); height = even(width * source_height / source_width)
RESIZE.when: the picture must become smaller / larger and keep its shape

FIT.keeps: every source pixel (scaled to fit inside, letterboxed / pillarboxed with pad_color)
FIT.target: width = params.width, else source_width when aspect <= source_aspect, else even(source_height * aspect); height = even(width / aspect)
FIT.when: a delivery aspect differs from the source and nothing may be lost

FILL.keeps: the centre of the picture (scaled to cover, centre-cropped); edges are lost
FILL.when: a delivery aspect differs from the source and a full frame matters more than the edges

ROTATE.changes: picture orientation only (a clockwise turn and/or a mirror); frame size changes only by the width x height swap a 90 / 270 turn implies -- never by scaling
ROTATE.keeps: every source pixel losslessly; no scaling, padding or cropping (like TRIM / CUT / SPEED / OVERLAY, unlike RESIZE / FIT / FILL)
ROTATE.target: width, height = source width, height (already measured as displayed); swapped when params.degrees is 90 or 270
ROTATE.when: a source was recorded or tagged with the wrong orientation, or needs mirroring, and no aspect or size change is wanted

CROP.changes: frame size, by cutting away everything outside one pixel rectangle
CROP.keeps: the pixels inside the rectangle exactly (no scaling, padding or stretching); the aspect becomes the rectangle's
CROP.target: width, height = params.width, params.height (even); x, y are offsets in the input frame as displayed, and the rectangle must lie inside it
CROP.when: the caller already knows the exact region to keep (a measured letterbox, a saved crop, a region it chose); FILL when the goal is an aspect ratio

rules: a source whose rotation metadata is ±90 / 270 is measured with width and height swapped (as the engine does)
CONCAT (ffmpeg-skill join.py): params.width x params.height; only one given -> the other from the first input's aspect (round); none -> the first input's frame; then floored to even

IMAGE_INSERT (ffmpeg-skill insert.py): params.width x params.height; only one given -> the other = even(given x the image aspect); none -> even(image width) x even(image height); the still is scaled to cover that frame and centre-cropped, never stretched

PUNCH_IN keeps the input frame: the window is floor_even(width / scale) x floor_even(height / scale), centred on the subject box, moved only as far as needed to stay inside the frame (even offsets), cropped (crop.py) and scaled back to the input frame (fit.py --fit crop: never stretched)

TRIM / CUT / SPEED / OVERLAY / ROTATE / FREEZE / REVERSE keep the input frame -- losslessly, no filter maths beyond a turn or a mirror for ROTATE, whose target frame is the source's width x height, swapped for a 90 / 270 degrees turn; an input with an odd width or height is refused before execution (INVALID_INPUT odd_frame) because the engine's encoders need even sizes
no operation stretches (distorts) the picture; anamorphic output is not provided
the normalized target frame is reported in plan.steps[].normalized and execution.operations[].normalized and verified on the output exactly

refused_before_execution: source with no video stream (audio-only files, corrupt containers): INVALID_INPUT no_video_stream
video source without a duration (a still image or a broken container declared as video): INVALID_INPUT no_duration
image source that does not decode to a frame: INVALID_INPUT image_undecodable

TRIM / CUT / SPEED / OVERLAY / ROTATE / FREEZE / REVERSE on an input whose frame has an odd width or height: INVALID_INPUT odd_frame (the encoder needs even sizes; RESIZE / FIT / FILL / CONCAT / IMAGE_INSERT normalize to even)
CONCAT of HDR and SDR inputs: INVALID_INPUT hdr_mismatch (the engine encodes from the first input's colour system)
unsupported input extension / output container: UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT
ranges beyond the input duration, transitions longer than half an input: INVALID_TIME_RANGE
CROP rectangle outside the input frame as displayed: INVALID_REQUEST crop_outside_frame
engine tool / encoder / filter missing: TOOL_ERROR (not retryable); FREEZE / REVERSE / IMAGE_INSERT / CROP need ffmpeg-skill/freeze / reverse / insert / crop, detected per checkout
normalized_by_skill: times in any accepted form -> exact rational seconds
target frame of RESIZE / FIT / FILL / CONCAT / CROP (frame_semantics)
target duration of SPEED (input duration / factor), FREEZE (input duration + hold) and IMAGE_INSERT (params.duration)
encoding profile -> typed engine flags (crf, preset)
audio expectation per operation (kept / added / none)
delegated_to_engine: scaling, padding, cropping filters and their exact pixel maths
constant-frame-rate conform of variable-frame-rate sources (a warning is reported)
resampling, silence insertion and stereo layout in CONCAT (an IMAGE_INSERT clip has no audio)
scaling / centre-cropping a still to its IMAGE_INSERT frame
silence under a FREEZE hold; reversing the audio with the picture in REVERSE
HDR sources encoded HEVC 10-bit (the output codec is hevc; a warning is reported)
audio codec / bitrate / sample rate (AAC 192 kb/s)
keyframe snapping for precision keyframe TRIM / CUT
copy-or-re-encode per cut for precision auto TRIM / CUT (cut.py --tolerance 0.2; the engine's choice is reported per cut)
which GOPs a precision smart TRIM / CUT re-encodes and whether the result verifies against the source (cut.py --smart; a fallback to a whole re-encode is reported with its reason)

by_stream.video_only: all operations allowed, OVERLAY included (ffmpeg-skill >=0.10.0 bounds the looped-image overlay with an explicit -t instead of -shortest); the output has no audio stream (validated)
by_stream.video_and_audio: all operations; the audio stream is kept (validated)
by_stream.audio_only: refused as a source (no_video_stream); audio-only editing is not provided
by_stream.image: OVERLAY.params.image only (png / jpg, alpha respected); an image in a video slot is DEPENDENCY_ERROR kind_mismatch; a video in OVERLAY.params.image is INVALID_INPUT overlay_video_layer (motion-graphics-skill video_overlay)
by_stream.mixed_audio_presence_in_concat: allowed; the engine inserts silence for the inputs without audio and the output has audio (validated)
by_stream.different_resolution_in_concat: allowed; conformed by params.mode to the normalized frame
by_stream.different_frame_rate_in_concat: allowed; conformed to params.fps or the first input's rate
by_stream.variable_frame_rate: allowed; conformed to constant fps by the engine (warning)
by_stream.hdr: allowed alone (output hevc, warning); not mixed with SDR in CONCAT
by_stream.rotation_metadata: honoured (a display matrix): the frame is measured as displayed; a legacy `rotate` tag is ignored by ffmpeg >= 5 and therefore by the probe
by_stream.odd_frame: RESIZE / FIT / FILL / CONCAT / IMAGE_INSERT normalize to even sizes; TRIM / CUT / SPEED / OVERLAY / ROTATE / FREEZE / REVERSE refuse it up front (odd_frame)
